gap: No result ChatGPT got says that the Kasa EP10 2-pack it recommended as 'best for simple timers' is missing from TP-Link's list of plugs with native Auto-Off (all Tapo plugs plus Kasa EP40M, KP125M and EP25 V2), so an EP10 can only shut itself off after each use through a Kasa Smart Action, which TP-Link says needs the plug online. It also doesn't say that the 'EP25 V2' on that list isn't among the hardware versions on TP-Link's US EP25 download page, which shows V1 only.
standout_why: Checked against the cited tapo.com/us/faq/83 (updated 09-29-2026) and tp-link.com/us/support/faq/947 (updated April 17, 2026), plus the uncited techgearden.com/best-smart-plugs (2026-11-03). FAQ 83 does print the native Auto-Off list, and FAQ 947 says plug auto-off built from Smart Actions needs internet. Each page holds one half, and neither applies them to the EP10 that ChatGPT picked. FAQ 947's own model list covers only EP40, HS300, KP115, KP200 and KP303 and doesn't name the EP10. ChatGPT's answer says 'Tapo also supports automatic shutoff', which implies Kasa doesn't, yet the EP25 V2 and KP125M are on the list. TechGearDen covers only countdowns for the EP10 and says nothing about Apple Home or Matter. None of the results ChatGPT got says that Apple Home needs a Matter hub to run the P125M remotely or in automations (tapo.com/us/faq/342).
decides: If the shopper wants a plug that turns off a set time after every use (a fan, coffee maker or charger), the pick should be the Tapo P125M (native Auto-Off, Matter, Apple Home) or the Kasa KP125M, not the EP10 2-pack. The EP10 is fine for fixed schedules and one-off countdowns. Anyone controlling the P125M from Apple Home needs an Apple TV-type hub to automate it or use it away from home; on iOS 18 it can be added without a hub, but then it only works locally. The Tapo app runs it with no hub.

Whether single-device schedules and countdown timers on Kasa or Tapo plugs keep running without internet: TP-Link FAQs 947, 83 and 2689 don't say. The EP25 and P125M user-guide PDFs that would cover it couldn't be read in this environment.
Whether the EP25 sold in the US (including the Cladby Home listing ChatGPT showed) is hardware V1 or V2: the US support page lists V1 only, and I found no maker document showing a US V2.
Whether Kasa EP10/EP25 can be added to and timed from the Tapo app: TP-Link FAQ 3762 ('How to Link Tapo with Kasa') appeared only in search results, and I didn't open it.
Maximum countdown length and maximum number of schedules per plug: none of the maker pages I opened state either.
